This game is what was missing on the Meta store: an INTENSE PvE Co-Op shooter with crossplay, including flat-screen PC players.

The invite for founders came along just as I was in the mood for a Doom-style game. The graphics are pretty simplistic but get the job done. I don't have huge amounts of experience with FPS so the "friendly bots" are a welcome addition, as are the target icons to guide you. The guns feel great to shoot and clearing every room with your "squad" is a feeling I haven't found in another game (not even the original Doom).  

Only 4 star because I'd like to see goodies to collect (the levels do feel a bit empty and there are lots of things glowing green that turn out to be nothing) and a greater variety of enemies. Otherwise, I have no regrets getting this game.

Exoshock is hands down one of the most exciting VR shooters I’ve played. The gunplay is incredibly satisfying, with weighty weapons, impactful hits, intense firefights, and an immersive sci-fi atmosphere that pulls you right into the action. It brings back the excitement of classic shooters like Halo and Doom while delivering something fresh that VR has been missing. The potential for co-op makes it even more exciting. You can tell there’s a lot of passion and care behind this game. If you’re looking for an adrenaline-pumping VR experience, Exoshock is absolutely worth checking out. Huge respect to the developers!

reviews.review_title: Strap In, Lock On, and Prepare for Chaos
reviews.review_description:
Exoshock has the potential to be something really special in VR.

The sci-fi setting, the atmosphere and the combat all come together to create an experience that makes you feel like you’re actually part of a futuristic military operation. There’s something particularly satisfying about being able to physically aim, reload and engage enemies in VR rather than just pressing buttons on a controller.

As a Founders Edition player, I’m excited to see where this game goes. There’s a solid foundation here, and I’m looking forward to seeing how the developers build on it with future updates and improvements.

It’s still early days, but Exoshock has already given me plenty of reasons to keep coming back. I’m looking forward to seeing what the future holds for this game.

developer_response.body:
Hey there, we deeply appreciate you sharing these comments. As an EA game we are constantly looking for bugs and issues to fix before our 1.0 launch.

A quick fix to prevent guns from spawning when reloading is to let go of all weapons with both hands. Then your mags should spawn correctly.

We are actively investigating the crash issue and hope to have a patch soon. Thank you for playing and sharing these comments!

reviews.review_title: An honest review on EXOSHOCK VR :)
reviews.review_description:
To start off, I'd like to thank the devs and producers of this game for distributing and making such a wonderful experience. I've been watching this game for a while on the shop and I'm very happy that Exoshock is out now. In this review I'll be going over some of the good things about this game and some things that could be fixed/improved.

 As for the good things, Exoshock has a fun gameplay loop (think of classic DOOM combined with 40k: Darktide), gritty science fiction aesthetics, a gradually unraveling lore that's woven into gameplay, easy to understand multiplayer system, and AWESOME gunplay. To be completely honest, this list doesn't do the experience of intercepting and breaching ships justice. You actually feel like a contracted soldier and not just a person larping as one. The firefights are visceral and high octane, but also high staked. Though its early access it has a LOT of potential and i recommend trying it out for yourself. HOWEVER, that does not mean this game is perfect.

 There are a few pressing issues/bugs I've noticed throughout playing the game. One of which is that guns will take ammo from another type of ammo instead of that weapons respective ammo well. For example, when reloading your rifle, instead of taking ammo from your rifle rounds it will take from the shotgun rounds (and vice versa), only the sidearms seem to work the best. Another thing i noticed is that when reloading you'll sometimes take out your third weapon + magazine in the same hand which can be confusing and irritating. Finally, I've observed that randomly you can get kicked out of the game entirely (in multiplayer servers, usually public servers but can sometimes be on private). Even if your ping is relatively good or tolerable. That's all i noticed so far, if you see anything else point it out :). 

The reason I've written this is because i wanted to provide a honest (or balanced depending how you look at it) perspective for people who want to come up with their own conclusion. Also i didn't want people to just see paid over-the-top bias. Any Anywho that's my review, have an amazing day (or week) and god bless (jesus loves you❤️)

reviews.review_title: This is what I've been waiting for
reviews.review_description: The day has finally come and the game is out. I've had my eye on this for quite a while and the developers have totally delivered. The PVE extraction is well done, what other games couldn't achieve for solo players, exoshock does it justice. Fast paced and exhilarating, I can't wait to spend more time with this game.

This is a game that has a very good foundation. If the developers can keep up with bug patches and adding new maps and content over time it can build a loyal community. Time will tell but just know you’ll be getting into a pretty unpolished version of the game where it sits right now. I want to see this game win because overall it is a great experience.

This game is 5/5 for me. I can clearly see the vision, and for an Early Access release the combat is already very fast-paced and intense. It feels different from a lot of other VR shooters in the best way.
The gunplay hits hard, the firefights move at a relentless pace, and every encounter keeps you on your toes. It’s chaotic, physical, and genuinely fun. Even at this stage it already delivers that “just one more run” feeling.
My only real wish is for more context and story — I want a clearer sense of why I’m fighting and a bit more world-building around the contracts and the corporation that owns you. That said, the core experience is so strong right now that it doesn’t hold the game back.
Hands down worth the $20. If you like intense, high-energy co-op (or solo with AI) sci-fi combat in VR, jump in. This one has serious potential and already feels special
